Carbon Dioxide Transport

Key Formulas/Values

Carbon dioxide transport occurs primarily through three mechanisms: diffusion, chemical buffering, and transport by the blood.

  • CO2 diffusion rate: 20-30 mL/min
  • CO2 buffering capacity: 20-30 mmol/L
  • CO2 transport by blood: 50-60% bound to hemoglobin, 20-30% dissolved in plasma, 10-20% bound to plasma proteins

Normal Ranges

Normal ranges for carbon dioxide transport-related values are as follows:

  • Arterial CO2 (PaCO2): 35-45 mmHg
  • Venous CO2 (PvCO2): 40-55 mmHg
  • Bicarbonate (HCO3-): 22-28 mmol/L

Classifications

Carbon dioxide transport can be classified based on its chemical form and mode of transport:

    • Bound CO2: bound to hemoglobin and plasma proteins
    • Free CO2: dissolved in plasma
    • Diffusion: CO2 diffuses from tissues to blood
    • Diffusion-convection: CO2 is transported by both diffusion and convection

Exam Traps

Common mistakes to avoid on the NORCET exam:

  • Confusing the diffusion rate of CO2 with the buffering capacity.
  • Overestimating the amount of CO2 bound to plasma proteins.
  • Failing to recognize the importance of CO2 transport in maintaining acid-base balance.
  • Not understanding the difference between bound and free CO2.
  • Misinterpreting the role of diffusion and convection in CO2 transport.
